raw_segments.text: I am so entirely convinced that the jury is preeminently a political institution that
I still consider it in this light when it is applied in civil causes.
Laws are always unstable unless they are founded upon the manners of a nation.
Manners are the only durable and resisting power in a people.
When the jury is reserved for criminal offenses, the people only witnesses its occasional action
The ordinary course of life goes on without its interference, and it is considered as
an instrument, but not as the only instrument of obtaining justice.
This is true affordery when the jury is only applied to certain criminal causes.
